title: Communications Legislation Amendment (Australian Content Requirement for Subscription Video On Demand (Streaming) Services) Bill 2025
short_title: Communications Legislation Amendment (Australian Content Requirement for Subscription Video On Demand (Streaming) Services) Bill 2025

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the bill text as introduced; not the record
sentences: The bill would require major subscription video on demand services to spend minimum amounts on new eligible Australian programs, with reporting and enforcement arrangements.
The requirement would equal 10% of program expenditure for Australia, with an option to use 7.5% of revenue derived from Australia instead.
Coverage would require at least 1 million paying Australian subscribers and other tests, excluding services dominated by user-generated content or with specified limited appeal.
changes: Eligible genres would include drama, documentaries, children’s, arts and educational programs, with qualifying New Zealand programs also included.
Services could carry surplus qualifying expenditure forward for up to two reporting years.
Providers of regulated services would have to submit annual compliance reports.
The Australian Communications and Media Authority could exempt classes of services from all or part of the scheme.
summary.affected: Providers of major subscription streaming services and the Australian Communications and Media Authority are affected.

speeches.speaker: Joanne Ryan
speeches.brief: Supported legislation requiring streaming platforms with more than one million Australian subscribers to invest 10 per cent of Australian sourced revenue in local content, arguing that Australian stories sustain national identity and support the screen sector.

speeches.speaker: Anika Wells
speeches.brief: Argued that the Communications Legislation Amendment (Australian Content Requirement for Subscription Video On Demand (Streaming) Services) Bill 2025 would require streaming services with one million or more Australian subscribers to invest at least 10 per cent of total expenditure or 7.5 per cent of revenue in new local content.

speeches.speaker: Julian Leeser
speeches.brief: Moved an amendment to the Communications Legislation Amendment (Australian Content Requirement for Subscription Video On Demand (Streaming) Services) Bill 2025, arguing that the Coalition has long supported the screen industry while the government is rushing the bill and risking financial harm to producers; the bill would impose reporting and investment obligations on major streamers, including 10 per cent of Australian program expenditure or 7.5 per cent of Australian revenue.

speeches.speaker: Jess Walsh
speeches.brief: Moved to suspend standing order 111 paragraphs (5) to (8) so four named bills could be considered during the period of sittings; the question was agreed to.
